articles.title: Presentation: Building GenAI Platform at DoorDash
articles.summary: Swaroop Chitlur and Sidd Kodwani share DoorDash’s journey building an internal GenAI platform. They discuss core architectural bets, transitioning from vendor-first setups to open-weights models, navigating LLM and agent gateways, and balancing accuracy, latency, and cost for over 5,000 internal users. articles.title: AI Agents Are Disrupting Open Source Security Disclosure
articles.summary: A recent article by Anil Madhavapeddy argues that AI agents can turn publicly available clues about software vulnerabilities into working exploits, reducing the effectiveness of traditional disclosure embargoes in open source projects. The author highlights the need for faster patching and release processes as the time between vulnerability disclosure and exploitation shrinks. By Renato Losio

articles.title: Istio 1.31 Adds Agentgateway Waypoints and Moves Release Artifacts off Google Cloud
articles.summary: Istio 1.31 adds agentgateway waypoints in ambient mode, with a canary configuration fix included in 1.31.1. It also ends the publication of images and Helm charts to Google Cloud, requiring repository migration ahead of the 13 October outage test and signing-key updates for teams verifying images. By Mark Silvester

articles.title: Want to Contribute to Open Source? Join Me in Building 8DoTs
articles.summary:
Did you know that the software we write has a real-world carbon footprint? 

As developers, we constantly profile our code for execution time and memory usage. But energy consumption remains largely invisible. That’s exactly what I’m trying to change with my open-source project, 8DoTs.


  
  
  What is 8DoTs?


8DoTs (internally structured as the dol8 Python package) is a command-line profiling tool designed to make energy consumption visible during software development. 

It reads hardware energy counters (RAPL - Running Average Power Limit) and thermal sensors directly from the Linux kernel

articles.title: Route planning for Southeast Asia without self-hosting OSRM
articles.summary:
Ask anyone who has run OSRM in production and they will tell you the same story: the routing engine is wonderful, and the server it runs on is a monster. The planet-wide graph wants 128 GB of RAM and a day of preprocessing. Even a Southeast Asia extract — the region many of us actually ship for — means tens of gigabytes of memory, multi-hour osrm-extract runs, and a recurring maintenance chore every time OpenStreetMap data is refreshed.

articles.title: Bank Reconciliation: The Fastest Way to Match Statements to Your Books
articles.summary:
Bank reconciliation is a fundamental financial process that ensures the cash balance in your accounting records matches the corresponding balance on your bank statement. While it might seem like a tedious chore, particularly for businesses handling a high volume of transactions, it's a critical practice for maintaining financial accuracy, detecting errors, and safeguarding against fraud.

articles.title: [R] Would you keep a robot demonstration if hand tracking missed the moment the plug went in?
articles.summary: Suppose you’re recording a human plugging a cable into a socket to collect demonstrations for robot learning. The hand tracker captures the approach accurately. Then occlusion causes the hand estimates to disappear during insertion. Tracking returns after the connector is already seated. The video still shows a completed action, but the pose labels have a gap exactly where alignment turns into contact.
